summary: `openssl-tls` trusts OpenSSL's default CA store in addition to the configured cluster CA
details:
With the `openssl-tls` connector, configuring a cluster CA (`certificate-authority`, `certificate-authority-data`, or the in-cluster `ca.crt`) did not limit which server certificates were trusted. The connector started from OpenSSL's default verify paths and added the configured roots to that store, so a server certificate chaining to any root in OpenSSL's default store passed trust validation. The certificate still had to be valid for the server name the client connects to. client-go and the `rustls-tls` connector trust only the configured CA.

An attacker on the path between the client and the apiserver who presents such a certificate, for example from a TLS inspection proxy whose root is installed on the machine, could complete the handshake and receive the client's requests, including bearer tokens.

This advisory covers the `openssl-tls` connector, added in 0.64.0, when a cluster CA is configured. The connector is used by `Client::try_default()`, `Client::try_from(Config)` and `ClientBuilder::try_from(Config)` whenever they select OpenSSL, by the `ConfigExt::openssl_https_connector`, `openssl_https_connector_with_connector` and `openssl_ssl_connector_builder` methods even when `rustls-tls` is also enabled, and since 4.2.0 for TLS to an `https://` proxy.

Which connector the constructors select depends on the version. Since 0.86.0, `rustls-tls` is the default and takes precedence when both features are enabled. From 0.71.0 to 0.85.x, `openssl-tls` was a default feature of `kube` (and of `kube-client` up to 0.82.2) and took precedence over `rustls-tls`. The `kube` crate re-exports `kube-client`, so the same `kube` versions are affected.

The flaw was corrected in 5.2.0 and 4.2.1 by installing a certificate store that holds only the configured root certificates. After upgrading, an `https://` proxy or a CA bundle that relied on OpenSSL's default store may need its CA added to the kubeconfig CA bundle. On older versions, switching the client to the `rustls-tls` connector avoids the issue.
